articleTitle: Agile-blended learning approach for Metropolitan learners in higher education: a systematic literature review
abstract: Agile-blended learning (AB learning) has gained growing attention as an innovative approach to blended learning. This paper aims to investigate the utilization of four key features of AB learning for Metropolitan learners, namely flexibility, learner autonomy, technology mediation, and collaboration. To conduct this study, the researchers followed PRISMA guidelines and analyzed 58 articles published between 2020 and 2024. The findings highlight the significance of flexibility, learner autonomy, technology mediation, and collaboration in AB learning. By incorporating these principles, educators can create dynamic learning environments that effectively cater to the needs of Metropolitan learners. This review contributes to the implementation of AB learning in metropolitan educational settings by providing valuable insights and recommendations.

articleTitle: Data Generation using a Probabilistic Auto-Regressive Model with Application to Student Exam Performance Analysis
abstract: Exam scores are usually the most important assessment criterion for evaluating students’ understanding of course materials and learning outcomes. Mid-term scores can serve as an indicator to predict exam scores because these assessments are generally common in the format of questions, closed-book assessments, and covering a variety of course topics. Machine learning algorithms have become a promising educational technology for forecasting student exam scores. If the prediction model suggests that a student is academically at risk, additional tutorial sessions and academic advice are potential follow-up actions. However, there are several research challenges: (i) mid-term scores are small-scale with limited samples, (ii) many physiological signals are required to supplement midterm and final exam scores as a multimodal problem, and (iii) insufficient investigation of the length of physiological signals. This paper employed a probabilistic autoregressive (PAR) model to generate Photoplethysmography (PPG) signals. A Wearable Exam Stress Dataset was used to benchmark the model. Results revealed that the PAR model can synthesize high-quality PPG signals in midterm and final exam scores to support educational research, particularly in the student exam performance analysis. Future research directions are suggested to further explore data generation research in education.

articleTitle: Gamification’s Impact on AI Education: An Empirical Analysis Using the GAFCC Framework
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence has made the world focused global attention on the construction of artificial intelligence courses. However, the artificial intelligence course faces many challenges in teaching, such as the complex content, theoretical abstraction and the disconnection from the practical application. Gamification learning has been widely proved to enhance learning outcomes, especially in skill acquisition and knowledge consolidation. Therefore, in order to solve these problems, this study employs a quasi-experimental research method, based on the gamification learning framework GAFCC, to deeply explore the application effect of gamification in artificial intelligence courses.

articleTitle: Tracking Students’ Self-Regulated Learning Behavior Patterns in a Flipped Engineering Course Using Process Mining: a Preliminary Study
abstract: As an important learning method, self-regulated learning (SRL) has been widely used in a variety of learning situations such as online and flipped learning. Exploring learners’ SRL behavior patterns has always been the focus of educational researchers. However, relatively fewer studies have focused on students’ SRL behavior patterns in flipped engineering courses. Since the critical role of SRL in the flipped classroom context, this study aimed to explore students’ self-regulated learning behavior patterns in a flipped engineering course of which the in-class learning was conducted in the way of Problem-Based Learning (PBL). Based on the process mining of 177 participants’ learning behavior data, the results showed that the dependence relationship between students’ SRL behavior was not completely consistent with the circular order in Pintrich’s SRL model, and students had different learning paths.

articleTitle: Virtual Simulation Aids for AI Curriculum Learning: A Quantitative Evaluation with the 5E Instructional Model
abstract: In this study, the teaching design of the artificial intelligence curriculum was carried out with reference to the 5E teaching model, using the virtual simulation platform as a teaching aid. In the teaching practice, students’ computational thinking, autonomous learning, and goal attainment were tested respectively, and the effects of the virtual simulation platform and the 5E teaching model on the learning outcomes of the AI curriculum were explored.

articleTitle: How Pre-service Teachers’ Basic Need Satisfaction Affect their AI Literacy in AI Introductory Courses? the Roles of Emotional Engagement and Self-regulated Learning
abstract: AI literacy is critical for both pre-service and inservice teachers. AI courses are an important way to develop pre-service teachers’ AI literacy. To explore how the basic needs satisfaction of pre-service teachers in AI courses affects their AI literacy, 498 pre-service teachers at N University in Northwest China participated in this survey. Path analyses, and mediating and moderating effects tests were conducted. We found that: (1) emotional engagement and self-regulated learning significantly and positively affected pre-service teachers’ AI literacy; (2) autonomy, competence, and self-regulated learning significantly and positively affected pre-service teachers’ emotional engagement; (3) emotional engagement fully mediated the relationship between autonomy, competence and AI literacy, (4) self-regulated learning significantly mediated the relationships between emotional engagement and AI literacy. Some implications for the development of pre-service teachers’ AI literacy in AI courses are suggested.

articleTitle: Project-Based Flipped Classroom Model Focusing on Outcome Communication and Evaluation
abstract: To address the limited effectiveness of the existing flipped classroom model in fostering students’ self-learning and teamwork abilities, a project-based flipped classroom model focusing on outcome communication and evaluation has been developed, which started with catering to students’ learning capabilities and guided by constructivist learning theory and student-centred teaching philosophy. This model, by offering practical projects and opportunities for collaborative learning, aims to stimulate students’ motivation and creativity, and cultivate their collaboration and problem-solving skills. Taking the teaching of C language loop programs as an example, the implementation process of the teaching is specifically elaborated, to provide references for the optimization and innovation of the flipped classroom model in the field of engineering education.

articleTitle: Embracing Technologies to Facilitate Student Learning and Future Readiness
abstract: Throughout history, events and technologies have often influenced teaching and learning, both in expected and unforeseen ways. The COVID-19 pandemic, while posing numerous challenges to student learning and development, also prompted the exploration of new teaching methodologies and deeper insights into faculty-student interactions. In today’s educational landscape, disruptive digital technologies such as learning management systems, student response devices, smartphones, and most recently, generative artificial intelligence (AI), have transformed teaching and learning. These technologies carry both potential benefits and risks, necessitating a careful balance that considers students’ significant reliance on digital tools. AI holds promise in enhancing student learning and fostering future readiness by offering novel approaches to active learning, authentic assessments, creativity, and scholarly pursuits. However, it also raises concerns regarding its potential for facilitating unethical practices, including cheating. This article examines the intertwined issues and challenges concerning technology and education, emphasizing how new technologies can enhance teaching, student learning, and assessment to better equip graduates for a rapidly evolving knowledge-based economy with new types of jobs and emerging career prospects. Faculty and universities’ responses to the challenges posed by new technologies will define their value and stature within society.

articleTitle: Research on “Scenarios-Resources-Interaction-Activities” (SRIA) Effective Strategies to Improve Virtual Simulation Learning Experience of Science in Primary School
abstract: Applying virtual simulation technology to advance primary school science education and focusing on improving the learning experience is of great significance to enhance teaching quality to the digital era. This study adopts the literature research method and theoretical deduction method to conduct research. According to the relevant literature at home and abroad, the connotation elements of primary school science virtual simulation learning experience were clarified, while the evaluation scale of primary school science virtual simulation learning experience was developed. Based on the Inquiry Learning Theory, combined with the general process of primary school science virtual simulation learning, the SRIA strategy to improve the learning experience of primary school science virtual simulation was preliminarily constructed. After two rounds of action research teaching practice, the SRIA strategy was continuously iteratively improved. Finally, the effect analysis showed that it could effectively improve the overall effect and various dimensions of the science virtual simulation learning experience in primary school. The innovation of this study is reflected in the first development of an assessment scale for the virtual simulation learning experience of primary school science. In general, the SRIA strategy can improve the virtual simulation learning experience of primary school science through theoretical and practical research.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Online Facilitators’ Inputs Based on Learning Analytics
abstract: Facilitators play a crucial role in offering learning support for highly interactive instructional activities within online courses. This study employed descriptive statistical analysis and Epistemic Network Analysis to analyze the observable behaviors and implicit cognitions of online facilitators. The results are visualized to illustrate the facilitators’ inputs. The findings address that online facilitators’ inputs align with the required support for the instructional activities designed in the course. However, variations exist in online facilitators’ time allocations for providing learning support. There are also significant differences in their perceptions of what elements should be included in the feedback provided for learners.

articleTitle: Grey Relational Analysis of the Impact of Classroom Teaching Behaviors and Student Engagement: An Example from a University Technology Theory Classroom
abstract: In the process of deepening the reform of higher education, the classroom plays an important role as the core teaching place. The application of teaching behaviors has a direct impact on the effectiveness of classroom teaching, and teaching behavior analysis, which improves the efficiency of teaching behaviors by exploring the laws of teaching behaviors of teachers and students, is an indispensable aspect in current classroom teaching research. In addition, the university technology theory classroom puts higher requirements on both teaching and learning than the basic education classroom. Based on the above background, the article formulated a teaching behavior table based on the previous research framework, calculated the students’ emotional engagement through the identification model of CoAtNet, and analyzed the teaching behaviors and student engagement in five university technology theory classrooms by combining the classroom observation method and grey relational analysis (GRA). The results of the study shows that the five teaching behaviors of Teaching, Board Writing, Reflection, Evaluation, Response and Teacher’s Question have a strong correlation with student engagement, which provides an important reference basis for the subsequent improvement of teaching behaviors to enhance students’ engagement.

articleTitle: Effects of Online Entertainment Modes and Duration on College Students’ Online Learning Burnout
abstract: Online learning burnout is an important factor affecting the quality of online learning and mental health of college students. Current research shows that online learning burnout is closely related to college students’ online entertainment modes (games, short videos, hit series and public opinion hot spots) and online entertainment duration. However, how online entertainment modes and duration affect online learning burnout of college students remains unknown. Therefore, this research explores the differences of online learning burnout among college students with different online entertainment modes and duration using difference analysis. The regression analysis is used to further explore the impact of online entertainment modes and duration on online learning burnout of college students. The results of this research shows that: (1) There are significant differences in college students’ online learning burnout between online entertainment modes. Specifically, “games” group is higher than the “public opinion hot spots” group, and the “short videos” group is higher than the “public opinion hot spots” group; (2) Online entertainment duration has a significant positive predictive effect on online learning burnout. The influence of online entertainment modes on college students’ online learning burnout is in the following order: “short videos”, “games”, “hit series”, “public opinion hot spots”.

articleTitle: A Virtual Reality Simulator for Learner Drivers to Prepare for Driving Test in Hong Kong
abstract: There is a significant number of candidates in Hong Kong awaiting their driving tests every year, yet the pass rates are notably low due to inadequate training time and high costs of practical training. To mitigate these issues, this paper presents the design of a cost-effective, immersive, and realistic driving test simulator. The simulator employs consumer-grade hardware, including a virtual reality (VR) headset and a driving wheelset, to familiarize users with the procedures and stress of an actual driving test, thereby enhancing their driving skills and increasing their likelihood of passing. The simulator features an authentic map for one of the driving test routes and is designed to mirror the actual exam procedure, providing a simulated environment for users to hone their driving skills and enhance their performance. We expect that the proposed approach will help train users’ higher-order driving skills and also provide valuable insights to education practitioners on integrating VR into practical skill training beyond driving.

articleTitle: A Study of Precision Instructional Interventions Based on Learner Profiles
abstract: Learner profiling, as a branch of big data learning analytics, enables the screening and integration of data resources and helps to realize accurate teaching. Goal-oriented development of accurate instructional interventions based on learner profiles requires systematic design. First, based on Bloom’s theory of categorization of cognitive goals in education, we developed a cognitive-oriented classification of behavioral goals and their data indicators, as well as a classification system for precise outcome goals. Then build a goal-oriented learner profile model, using learners’ learning styles, behavioral characteristics, and outcome characteristics as the basis for drawing profiles, accurately differentiating students, and diagnosing teaching problems. Then, based on the results of learner profiling, design precise teaching intervention strategies, conduct multiple rounds of expert consultation, and finally form precise teaching intervention strategies, and then carry out precise teaching interventions. The results of practical application show that accurate teaching intervention based on learner profiles is effective in improving behavioral and outcome goals.

articleTitle: A Symmetric Metamorphic Relations Approach Supporting LLM for Education Technology
abstract: Question-Answering (Q&A) educational websites are widely used as self-learning platforms, and pre-trained large language models (LLMs) play a crucial role in maintaining content quality. Despite their usefulness, LLMs still fall short of human performance. To tackle this issue, we propose leveraging symmetric Metamorphic Relations (MRs) to enhance LLMs’ performance by improving their machine common sense. The goal is to ensure that learners receive more relevant content. This work presents an empirical experiment using one specific symmetric MR, three LLMs, and a publicly available dataset of labelled Stack Overflow data. We employ the symmetric MR to generate training data that augments the machine common sense of LLMs. Additionally, we prepare a separate set of training data consisting of labelled Stack Overflow data for comparison purposes. By comparing the results of a common ability test and the predictions made by LLMs trained with different training datasets, we can assess the potential practicality of our proposed approach. Our experimental results demonstrate that a Bert-based LLM trained with MR-generated data outperforms a Bert-based LLM trained solely with regular labelled data. This outcome highlights the effectiveness of symmetric MRs in enhancing LLMs’ performance by improving their machine common sense. Subsequent studies can extend our approach to other domains related to education technology and explore additional MRs to further enhance the study experience of students.

articleTitle: Assessing the Applicability of the CDIO Model to AI Curriculum in K-12 Education: A Quasi-Experimental Study with Eighth Graders
abstract: The nurturing of artificial intelligence (AI) professionals is garnering escalating focus within global national strategies. However, there persists a paucity of appropriate pedagogical paradigms for AI curricula within K-12 educational models. This study explores the integration of the CDIO model into AI instruction in K-12 institutions and evaluates its influence on student performance. Employing a Quasi-Experimental design, the study targeted a specific AI lesson ‘Designing My Unmanned Supermarket’, Lesson 5 in the first book of Grade 8. A comparative analysis was conducted between a control group and an experimental group.” The results demonstrate that the teaching model based on the CDIO model has a positive impact on students’ learning outcomes and comprehensive competence. A comparative analysis was conducted between a control group and an experimental group.

articleTitle: Academic Emotions and Learning Engagement in Synchronous Delivery Classroom: Mediating Effects of Self-efficacy and Learning Motivation
abstract: The synchronous delivery classroom (SDC) has realized the sharing of high-quality education resources between rural and urban areas, which plays a crucial role in promoting the comprehensive development of rural school students. Due to the separation of physical spaces between teachers and students in SDC, it results in a lower level of learning engagement among students. Academic emotions play an important role in improving students’ learning engagement. The purpose of this study is to explore the impact of academic emotions on students’ learning engagement in SDC. A sample of 214 rural school students in China participated in this study. Analysis of the collected data revealed that: (1) Positive emotions experienced by students in SDC were generally higher than negative emotions. (2) Positive emotions significantly and positively predicted learning engagement, while the predictive effect of negative emotions was not significant. (3) Self-efficacy and learning motivation played parallel mediating roles in the relationship between positive emotions and learning engagement. These findings can provide new ideas on improving students’ learning engagement in SDC.

articleTitle: Effects of Blended Learning by Gamification on Chinese College Students’ College English Learning Engagement and Foreign Language Anxiety
abstract: This research explores the impact of integrating gamification into blended learning on Chinese college students’ College English learning engagement and foreign language anxiety(FLA). Using a mixed-methods approach, the study demonstrates positive outcomes. Quantitative data reveal a significant increase in learning engagement and a notable decrease in foreign language anxiety. Qualitative insights highlight students’ positive perceptions of gamified elements, emphasizing heightened motivation and interest. The findings contribute practical implications for educators seeking to enhance language learning experiences through innovative strategies.

articleTitle: Enhancing Socially Shared Regulation and Equalized Discussions in Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning: A Role Scripts Approach
abstract: This study investigates the impact of role fixation (RF) and role rotation (RR) scripts on learners’ socially shared regulation (SSR) in computer-supported collaborative learning (CSCL) environments. The research involved 25 undergraduate students from a university in central China, divided into RF and RR groups for an eight-week collaborative learning activity focused on the Computer Networks course. Data were collected through self-report questionnaires and online discussions platform. Findings indicate that RF groups exhibited significantly higher levels of SSR and more balanced discussions compared to RR groups. RF groups fostered a more evenly distributed interaction network, enhancing cooperation and sharing. These results underscore the effectiveness of role fixation scripts in promoting SSR and improving collaborative learning outcomes.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a graphical programming class for computational thinking in elementary schools
abstract: As the process of artificial intelligence progresses, it is recognized that computational thinking is one of the basic skills for understanding and solving problems and one of the core literacies of the IT discipline. There are various ways to develop students’ computational thinking, and at the primary and secondary school levels, graphical programming classes are an important way to do so. This study establishes a framework for an instructional program aimed at developing students’ computational thinking skills based on elementary school graphic programming classes. Combining curriculum standards, graphic programming standards for youth programming skills, and International Computational Thinking Challenge standards, relevant teaching cases are designed to foster students’ computational thinking and promote the development of computational concepts, computational practices, and computational concepts.

articleTitle: Digital Teaching Platform for Middle School Physical Education: Case Study on Tennis Lesson
abstract: In the context of intelligent education, this paper explores the application of digital physical education (PE) in middle schools through the example of a digital tennis teaching platform. Firstly, the overall framework of digital tennis teaching is established, and the digital teaching scheme is designed based on the two key parts from the guidelines of United States Professional Tennis Association, which focus directly on tennis skills. Secondly, wearable motion capture devices are developed to capture and display the character animation of students and coaches in real time, while a stroke simulator provides feedback. Subsequently, the detailed analysis methods of tennis strokes including the tennis racket angle, kinetic chain diagram, contribution velocity and time coordination are proposed and visualized on the software interface to teach and guide tennis stroke motion. Finally, a tower defense game to be both educational and entertaining is designed, aimed at enhancing students’ tennis control ability. The teaching method proposed in this paper offers a novel PE mode for middle school students by integrating artificial intelligence into traditional PE, which is able to gather extensive data on students’ physical health, paving the way for future personalized teaching strategies.

articleTitle: GPT and Translation: A Systematic Review
abstract: Despite the growing use of GPT for translation, little research has analyzed studies on GPT and translation. This paper aims to provide a systematic literature review to explore the overall trend and summarize the major benefits and limitations of using GPT for translation based on 16 reviewed papers. The results demonstrate that there has been a significant increase in the number of publications, particularly in the field of translation quality of the European languages. Most studies used a quantitative method, and the findings mostly suggest that GPT-generated translations are on par with human translations and perform better than neutral machine translation outputs. GPT can accurately translate cultural texts, complex structures, and advanced linguistic features, such as poetry, humor, and pun. It is also found that GPT can be effectively used not only for translation but also for post-editing and translation evaluation, leading to new challenges and ethical concerns. This research highlights the changing roles of the key stakeholders and concludes with some direction for future studies.

articleTitle: A Review on Information and Communications Technology in Higher Education: Learning Theories and Applications
abstract: Previous research focused on innovative technologies in higher education, neglecting educational gains. Insufficient data exists to support the effectiveness of educational technology due to reliance on student satisfaction surveys. Lack of defined theories and their application hinders theory advancement. A review study examined 96 filtered studies from 1998 to 2020, mapping educational technology applications to theories and suggesting future research directions.

articleTitle: The Construction and Application of Prompt Framework for Improving College Students’ Human-Machine Synergy Learning Ability with Generative AI
abstract: Generative AI-supported human-machine synergy (HMS) learning is emerging as a new form of learning. Prompt, as the supporting scaffold, significantly impacts the synergy effects between learners and generative AI. To investigate the role of prompt framework in improving college students’ human-machine synergy learning ability (HMS learning ability), this study conducted the methods of literature research, theoretical deduction, and quasi-experimental research. Guided by the theories of distributed cognition, information processing and the cooperative principle of conversation, this study clarified the connotation and core dimensions of HMS learning ability, analyzed the HMS learning process with generative AI, explored the impact of prompt framework on college students’ human-machine synergy learning ability and finally, constructed the “GCRET” prompt framework to enhance college students’ human-machine synergy learning ability, and its effectiveness was verified through the Human-Machine Synergy Learning Ability Scale and students’ project practice report. According to the effect analysis, the constructed “GCRET” framework significantly enhanced college students’ HMS learning ability, especially HMS evaluation and judgment ability. The researchers hope that this study could provide theoretical and practical references for further exploring the HMS learning with generative AI.

articleTitle: Engaging Student Engagement in Blended Learning Environments through Integration of Small Private Online Courses
abstract: In recent years, blended learning has been increasingly adopted in higher education, with its benefits well-documented. However, little research has explored the student learning experience when integrating Small Private Online Courses (SPOCs) into specific university courses. This study investigates undergraduate students’ perceptions of blended learning through the incorporation of SPOCs into the ‘Learning Science and Technology’ curriculum. Data were collected using questionnaires and interviews to assess students’ experiences of the blended courses and perceptions of its implementation. The findings revealed that students viewed the blended learning experience and its implementation positively, contributing significantly to their engagement in the courses. Additionally, student’s interview responses predominantly reflected a favorable attitude toward the use of SPOCs within traditional classroom settings. This research provides a concrete empirical example of effective blended learning practices using SPOCs in a university context.

articleTitle: The Relationship Between ICT Utilization and Digital Literacy: The Moderating Role of Parental Educational Level
abstract: This study explored the relationship between information and communications technology (ICT) utilization, parental educational level and digital literacy. The survey results from a total of $\mathbf{8, 8 8 4}$ primary school students from four provinces in southern China showed that ICT utilization was significantly and positively correlated with digital literacy, and that parental educational level was significantly and positively correlated with digital literacy. The results of the moderating effect showed that mothers’ educational level played a significant positive moderating role between ICT utilization and digital literacy, and ICT utilization positively predicted digital literacy more for students with high level of mothers’ education; however, father’s educational level did not play a moderating role between ICT utilization and digital literacy. Finally, this study put forward some recommendations for promoting students’ digital literacy according to the results and provided directions for future research.

articleTitle: A Preliminary Analysis of AI Chatbots for Individualized Nutrition Advice
abstract: The rapid development of AI chatbots receives increasing recognition in different applications. Nutrition is an important topic because the general public values health. A lot of general nutrition advice can be found on the Internet. However, many people or patients desire individualized nutrition advice from dietitians. Given the availability of various free or low-cost AI chatbots, attention is drawn to individualized nutrition advice using AI chatbots. This research studied three common AI chatbots: ChatGPT-3.5, YouChat, and Microsoft Bing. The results of selected prompts are investigated and compared. Comments from dietitians on the limitations of AI chatbots are also shared. Further research is needed to investigate the design of prompts, i.e., asking appropriate questions with a good level of detail to the AI chatbots and having follow-up conversations to obtain better individualized nutrition advice.

articleTitle: Research on the Impact of Social Presence, Academic Self-efficacy, and Flow Experience on Students’ Learning Engagement in Blended Synchronous Learning
abstract: Blended synchronous learning combines traditional face-to-face teaching and online learning, aiming to provide a flexible and diversified learning experience and enhance the learning effect of students. The purpose of this study is to explore how students’ social presence, academic self-efficacy, and flow experience affect students’ learning engagement in the blended synchronous learning environment. Through literature review and comprehensive analysis, research has found that social presence, academic self-efficacy, and flow experience have a significant direct impact on students’ learning engagement. In addition, social presence has an indirect promoting effect on students’ learning engagement through academic self-efficacy and flow experience. This study provides theoretical support and practical guidance for the teaching practice of blended synchronous classrooms, which helps improve students’ learning experience and effect.

articleTitle: A Scoping Review of Educational Use of Spherical Video-based Virtual Reality: Future Directions in Research
abstract: In recent years, there has been a steady rise in reviews exploring the application of Spherical video-based virtual reality (SVVR) in education. Meanwhile, there has been a growing number of empirical research focused on the educational use of SVVR. This review aims to provide a brief overview of the trends in this domain and to summarize new research directions. Thirty-eight articles published in the recent five years (2019-2023) were identified for this review, and three general future research directions are proposed to foster continued research and development in SVVR for educational applications.

articleTitle: The mediating role of information literacy on reducing academic stress and burden for primary school students
abstract: In 2021, the Chinese government implemented the “Double Reduction” policy, aiming to reduce the burden of homework and off-campus training for students in compulsory education. To verify the effectiveness of this policy, this study tracked and surveyed 5774 primary school students in Wuhan from the year of 2020 for three consecutive years, and conducted the repeated measurement, to explore the changes in their academic and burden, as well as the moderating effect of information literacy. The results showed that students’ academic burden and stress significantly decreased over the three years. These students could be divided into two clusters: high information literacy and low information literacy. Students with high information literacy had better stress reduction and burden reduction abilities. The results provide new way to enhance the implementation of the “Double Reduction” policy, reminding teachers to pay more attention to improving students’ information literacy, so as to better reduce their burden while promoting their overall development.

articleTitle: Research Trends of Artificial Intelligence in Language Education: A Bibliometric Review
abstract: With the rapid development of society and technology, the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become increasingly pivotal in a variety of fields, particularly in language education. The integration of AI with language pedagogy, through the utilization of natural language processing and machine learning algorithms, offers an enhanced and interactive learning experience, thereby fulfilling the needs of language learners and contributing to the expansion of academic research. This study conducts a bibliometric analysis on AI in language education domain, presents primary publication sources, and then identifies the important research topics within this burgeoning field. Finally, suggestions on highlighting research on cognitive emotions, interdisciplinary studies, and the establishment of an ethical framework are proposed for future scholarly endeavors.

articleTitle: Impact of the BOPPPS Model Integrated with Game Elements on Learning Effect in Information Technology Courses for Junior Students
abstract: In the information technology course, students do not actively participate in the class, so this study designed learning activities based on the BOPPPS model integrated with game elements. To verify the effectiveness of this model, we conducted a quasi-experiment with a sample of 86 junior students in two classes. The results showed that the experimental group with the BOPPPS model integrated with game elements was superior to the control group with the traditional teaching model in terms of knowledge, learning engagement and self-efficacy. Therefore, in information technology courses, the BOPPPS model integrated with game elements could be useful to improve the learning effect of students.

articleTitle: Study on the influencing factors of junior high school students’ cognitive load in the smart classroom environment
abstract: To investigate the influencing factors of junior high school students’ cognitive load in the smart classroom environment (SCE), a questionnaire survey was conducted, with eighth-grade junior high school students in a public school in Northwest China as the subjects. Additionally, structural equation modeling was used to verify and analyze the inherent logical relationships among self-efficacy, teacher support, facilitating conditions, and students’ cognitive load in the SCE. The results showed that students’ self-efficacy, teacher support, and facilitating conditions had significant negative effects on students’ extraneous load and significant positive effects on students’ germane load. In addition, facilitating conditions were found to have a significant positive effect on teacher support in the SCE.

articleTitle: The Theory of Facilitating Task Performance in the Presence of a Virtual Audience
abstract: In the present study, the author investigated the effects of the presence of the virtual audience on task performance of different tasks (easy tasks and difficult tasks) and anxiety levels, including trait anxiety and state anxiety. Social facilitation was observed in the easy tasks when the virtual audience was present, whereas social inhibition was not observed in the difficult tasks. These findings differed from those observed by the human audience. To investigate the reason for these results, the author analyzed the participants’ trait anxiety before the experiment and state anxiety after the experiment. The results showed that state anxiety elicited by the virtual audience was significantly lower than that elicited by the human audience, elevated state anxiety might result in decreased task performance.

articleTitle: Effects of digital game-based learning on students’ digital commerce literacy and learning engagement
abstract: The Internet has become an indispensable part of people’s daily life, and online shopping has brought a lot of convenience to people. However, there are online fraud, information leakage and other security risks in online shopping. To ensure that adolescents are able to spot these risks and enhance their digital commerce literacy, this study selected 84 students from YS Primary School to conduct a four-week digital citizenship education program and investigate the effects of digital game-based learning (DGBL) on their digital commerce literacy and learning engagement. The statistics showed that students who participated in DGBL demonstrated higher digital commerce literacy and performed better on learning engagement than those who learned in traditional way.

articleTitle: Generating Multivariate Exam Scores using Copulas and Socioeconomic Factors
abstract: Final exams are essential to assessing students’ level of understanding of the course materials and evaluating their achievements in the learning outcomes. Many factors may have affected their performance throughout the courses. These are personal-, social-, and economic-related. Student Exam Performance Datasets are usually small-scale. The nature of a typical dataset comprises a small class size and few assessment components, and the students and parents may refuse to disclose and share too much personal information. This paper proposes a copula-based data generation algorithm that provides additional training data for the datasets. The algorithm is evaluated based on eight aspects: diagnostic, data quality, missing value similarity, statistic similarity, category coverage, range coverage, new row synthesis, and column comparison.

articleTitle: The Impact of Mobile AR Application on Learning Motivation in Biological Learning Based on The ARCS Model
abstract: Augmented reality (AR) technology can address the challenges in implementing experimental teaching in underserved areas. To examine AR’s impact on biology learning, we developed a mobile AR application for biological teaching and conducted experiments in a remote Chinese middle school, using the ARCS learning motivation model. Twenty-six students in the control group (CG) received traditional teaching, while 23 students in the experimental group (EG) used the AR software. Results reveal that post-AR teaching, students with higher motivation showed significantly improved academic performance. Moreover, students in EG demonstrated higher motivation compared to students in CG, with EG’s academic improvement significantly surpassing CG’s. The results of interview indicated that the teaching with AR fosters better cognitive construction and emotional acceptance than traditional methods.

articleTitle: Research on Feedback Teaching Mode to Enhance Student Engagement Based on Smart Paper-pen System
abstract: Along with the emergence of emerging technologies such as big data, many tools have been developed to optimize classroom instruction. Student non-engagement is one of the most immediate and ongoing issues in educational practice. In order to promote student engagement in the classroom, this study analyzes the relationship between feedback and student engagement, on the basis of which a feedback teaching model based on smart paperpen system to improve student engagement is constructed and the effect is verified in a middle school in Guangzhou, China. After measuring and analyzing the data several times with the help of SPSS, it was finally found that following the model for teaching and learning, student engagement in the classroom was greatly improved. Therefore, this study can provide a model and experience for future teachers to apply the smart paper-pen system for feedback teaching in the classroom.

articleTitle: A multi-dimensional analytics approach to course evaluation
abstract: This paper presents a multi-dimensional analytics approach to course evaluation to facilitate the monitoring and enhancement of teaching and learning quality. A course evaluation platform has been developed, which utilises data from student feedback surveys and course grades for various levels of data analysis to satisfy the diverse needs and interests of different stakeholders. The platform supports trend and pattern analyses regarding the dimensions of students’ satisfaction and course grades across academic terms. By enabling users to find out efficiently and effectively the relationships between courses, instructors, student satisfaction, and course grades, the course evaluation platform facilitates users to gain insights and take suitable follow-up actions for course and teaching improvement.

articleTitle: Does computational thinking really have an impact on academic performance? A systematic review
abstract: This study is a systematic review of the effects of computational thinking on students’ academic performance from 2006 to 2023. The main purpose of this study is to explore whether computational thinking can promote students’ academic performance and the characteristics of such research. After literature collection and screening from three databases, a total of $\mathbf{2 3}$ articles were included. According to the coding table, the literature was coded in five aspects, including basic information, sample, research, computational thinking and academic performance. Then, the publication trend, research types, effect results, computational thinking measurement and the characteristics of academic achievement evaluation of the impact of computational thinking and academic achievement are reviewed. It is found that computational thinking has a better effect on students’ academic achievement, and finally some suggestions are put forward.

articleTitle: Transitioning STEAM Workshop with Experiential Activities from Face-to-Face to Online
abstract: Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics (STEAM) education aims to promote interdisciplinary learning and cultivate students’ problem-solving and innovation skills through a robust emphasis on experiential learning. However, the global pandemic has significantly affected education, halting traditional face-to-face teaching and rendering hands-on teaching activities and resources fail. To mitigate these challenges, we transitioned science workshops and hands-on experiences from a classroom to an online format. This shift enabled continuous learning during class suspension and facilitated uninterrupted practical, experiential learning for students. This paper delineates the context of the transition, the methodology employed in the transition process, and the implications for the future development of learning and teaching materials.

articleTitle: Utilizing Virtual Reality and Generative AI Chatbot for Job Interview Simulations
abstract: Stress and anxiety experienced by interviewees, particularly fresh graduates, would significantly impact their performance in job interviews. Due to the increased affordability and user-friendliness of virtual reality (VR), VR has seen a surge in its application within the educational sector. This paper presents the design and implementation of a job interview simulation system, leveraging VR and a generative AI chatbot to provide an immersive environment for computer science graduates in Hong Kong. The system aims to help graduates practice and familiarize themselves with various real-world scenarios of a job interview in English, Mandarin, and Cantonese, tailored to the unique language requirements of Hong Kong’s professional environment. The system comprises three core modules: a mock question and answer reading module, an AI speech analysis module, and a virtual interview module facilitated by the generative AI chatbot, ChatGPT. We anticipate that the proposed simulator will provide valuable insights to education practitioners on utilizing VR and generative AI for job interview training, extending beyond computer science graduates.

articleTitle: Using 3D Virtual and Physical Robot Alone or Together-Which Works Better for Learning engagement and Computational Thinking
abstract: With the development of virtual reality technology, 3D virtual robots are increasingly used in primary school robot programming teaching. Therefore, in this study, 64 fifth-grade students were divided into two groups, and the experimental research method was used to investigate which method is more conducive to improving students’ learning engagement and computational thinking by combining or separately using 3D virtual robots and physical robots in robot programming courses. The results show that the combined use of 3D virtual and physical robots in a robot programming course improves students’ Programming self-efficacy scale and learning engagement, thus improving students’ computational thinking.

articleTitle: The Construction of a COPAE Project-based Learning Model for Primary School Chinese Language Empowered by Digital Intelligence Technology
abstract: This study addresses the practical need for classroom reform in the context of dual-new backgrounds. By utilizing methods such as literature research, theoretical deduction, and action research, a project-based COPAE learning model for elementary Chinese language education, empowered by digital intelligence technology, is developed. The approach is guided by big concepts that involve refining the project’s big concept, determine the project objectives, designing project implementation programs, organizing project-based learning activities, and conducting project effectiveness evaluations to facilitate implementation. Through three rounds of iterative improvements using action research, the analysis of outcomes suggests that the COPAE model effectively enhances students’ learning interests, encourages creative output, and thereby promote the development of core literacy in Chinese language education.

Author Keywords: Primary School Chinese Language Project-based Learning

articleTitle: The construction and application of precise teaching mode based on educational big data
abstract: The mastery of knowledge points by students is not only an important indicator of their academic performance but also a crucial avenue for personalized learning. Based on an analysis of the current state of high school chemistry teaching in China, this study integrates a precision teaching platform as a data support for instruction and proposes a precision teaching model grounded in educational big data. Through the excavation of student test scores, we accurately analyze each student’s knowledge mastery based on their exam performance, enabling personalized learning. Furthermore, by analyzing test scores, we achieve precision teaching by precisely assessing each student’s knowledge mastery. We take two classes in the first year of high school in a school in Guizhou as experimental subjects. With one class as the experimental group and the other class as the control group, the experimental group used the platform technology to carry out precise teaching in chemistry exercise classes and the control group carried out traditional lecture teaching, and the results of the experiment were subsequently processed and analysed by collecting and analysing the results of the two chemistry exams of the two classes. Finally, it was found that the use of big data in education for precision teaching can address the problems and needs of teachers who are unable to meet the differences in the levels of students at different levels of instruction. This provides a new perspective for chemistry exercise review classes, optimizing teaching effectiveness and enhancing the efficiency of both teaching and learning.

articleTitle: Design and empirical research of critical thinking training model based on digital science argument mapping
abstract: As the core competence of modern learners, critical thinking, which is based on reasoning and evidence, is urgently needed by learners, so it is indispensable to help learners develop their critical thinking. The science argument mapping provides a new research direction and thinking perspective for the promotion of critical thinking, especially in daily classroom teaching, science argument mapping is used to support the training of learners’ critical thinking, to achieve the development of critical thinking. This study combines scientific argument map tools, argument teaching, curriculum teaching, and related theories to build a critical thinking training model based on a scientific argument map, and expounds on the model and the application of a scientific argument map. Meanwhile, this training model is verified through quasi-experimental research. The results show that the cultivation model based on a scientific argument map plays a positive role in promoting critical thinking ability and emotional tendency.

articleTitle: Intelligent Integration of Industry and Education in Innovative Talent Training
abstract: To meet the demand for talent training in the green, intelligent, and integrated development of the petrochemical industry, this article explores the training of innovative talents through intelligent integration of industry and education. Artificial intelligence and petrochemical engineering featured “intelligent oil” class is proposed to train talents with engineering practice ability and technological innovation ability. The “dual system” talent training model and the “target problem oriented” curriculum system are implemented in the talent training process, and the intelligent teaching system is introduced through a case study of the course titled “Principles of Chemical Engineering”.

articleTitle: Research on the Syllabus Structure and Connotation of Blended Learning Curriculum Based on OBE Theory
abstract: In recent years, the quality of syllabus has increasingly gained attention from educational management departments, teachers, and students. Based on literature research, this article outlines the essence of the syllabus and elaborates the basic rules for curriculum development for blended learning courses based on OBE. Drawing from recent years’ practices in syllabus development, it refines the structural framework and key elements of the teaching syllabus for OBE-based blended learning courses. An online syllabus compilation software has been developed to provide teachers with a framework for designing OBE-based blended learning course syllabus, thus enhancing the efficiency of syllabus compilation. Through pre-set modules, demos, and explanatory content based on the theory research, this software deepens teachers’ understanding of the teaching syllabus and facilitates students’ better comprehension and utilization of the syllabus for better understanding and learning of the course.

articleTitle: Research on Teaching Activities in University Blended Technology Development Courses with Support from Generative Virtual Digital Humans
abstract: In the current educational environment, blended courses have been widely used in university classrooms. With the advancement of AI technology, generative virtual digital humans are gradually being introduced into the education field. However, there are few studies combining the two. To this end, this study designed an experiment to compare the effects of a blended course based on generative virtual digital humans and a traditional blended course. We selected 60 students, 30 of whom participated in a blended course based on generative virtual digital humans (experimental group), and the other 30 students took a traditional blended course (control group). Before and after the experiment, we conducted tests on the cognitive load, flow state, etc. of the two groups of students, and collected data related to academic achievement. Research results show that students in the experimental group are better than those in the control group in terms of cognitive load, flow state, and academic achievement, indicating that blended courses based on generative virtual digital humans have significant effects on reducing cognitive load and improving learning experience and effects. Advantage. This provides a useful reference for future educational innovation, helps promote the development and improvement of educational technology, and improves the quality and effectiveness of education.

articleTitle: Development of a Formative Assessment System for Reports Using Large Language Models and Rubrics
abstract: The formative use of rubrics has gained attention in education, particularly in first-year university report writing. This is because rubrics can clarify learning objectives, provide feedback, and promote self-regulated learning. Integration with Large Language Models (LLMs) can significantly enhance this practice. LLMs can interpret and process language-based reports and rubric criteria with high accuracy. This enables objective assessments aligned with rubric standards and offers specific advice for report improvement. These characteristics can assist in overcoming challenges associated with self-use of rubrics in independent study scenarios where feedback from teachers is unexpected or difficult to obtain. This study introduces our past practices using rubric-embedded prompts to improve students’ writing skills and presents an overview of the “Report Advisor,” a system developed using OpenAI’s GPTs platform to address technical issues, along with a brief evaluation of its feedback validity. This study presents several limitations and suggests avenues for future research in this area.

articleTitle: The impact of STEM Courses and STEM Interests on the STEM Major Intention of middle school students with the moderating effect of Career Planning Courses
abstract: The cultivation of STEM Major Intention among secondary school students is crucial for fostering future STEM talents. This study aims to investigate the factors that influence students’ intention to pursue a STEM Major Intention, considering both school curriculum offerings and personal factors, employing Structural Equation Modeling analysis. A questionnaire survey was conducted with 425 middle school and high school students in a STEM demonstration area. The findings indicate that STEM Course Offerings, STEM Interests, and the availability of Career Planning Courses significantly impact their STEM Major Intention. Specifically, a greater abundance of STEM Courses leads to higher Interest in STEM among students, stronger STEM Interest translates to a higher STEM Major Intention, and Career Planning Courses can moderate the relationship between STEM Interests and STEM Major Intentions. The reasons for these results and recommendations for fostering STEM Major Intention will be explored further.

articleTitle: Objectives, Methods, and Challenges of Applying Intelligent Assessment in Education: A systematic review
abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence technology, traditional assessment has been gradually replaced by intelligent assessment. This study systematically reviews research on the use of intelligent assessment in education between 2015 and 2024. 51 papers were finally included and analyzed for the objectives, methods, and challenges of adopting intelligent assessment in educational activities. The results show that the goals of intelligent assessment in education can be grouped into three categories: 1) assessment of students’ competence and knowledge levels; 2) assessment of students’ personality and mental health; and 3) assessment of teaching and learning processes. The studies reviewed used a range of assessment methods to achieve their objectives. These encompassed process-based, student competency-based, and dynamism-based approaches, as well as social media text-based, audio, and video-based assessment methods. Additionally, they employed student assessment-based and teacher performance assessment-based methods. These methods involved designing algorithms, application systems, or scale assessment tools to effectively measure and evaluate various aspects of learning and teaching. The challenges were present in three areas: data collection and processing, adaptation of assessment models, and accuracy and interpretability of assessment results.

articleTitle: Is Multimodal Dictation Practice More Effective than Audio-only Dictation?
abstract: This research explores the impact of multimodal dictation on English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners’ comprehension, retention, and transcription performance. Despite growing interest in multimodal learning, studies primarily focus on input presentation and sequencing, neglecting dictation integration. This study involved 62 Chinese high school students randomly assigned to audio-only or video groups. The video group underwent dictation tasks with accompanying visuals. Outcomes were assessed through dictation tests, comprehension post-tests, recalls, questionnaires, and interviews. Results showed superior performance by the video group, indicating that multimodality enhances dictation by fostering understanding. Participant feedback supported multimodal dictation for richer contexts, aiding inferences, reducing cognitive load, and improving comprehension. These findings advocate for multimodal dictation in enhancing EFL learners’ transcription and emphasize considering individual differences and video characteristics in its application.

articleTitle: A systematic review of theories, themes, and methods related to online course review analysis
abstract: The feedback mechanism known as course reviews within massive open online courses (MOOCs) has spurred the creation of extensive textual feedback. This information, encompassing not just learners’ perspectives, thoughts, and emotions regarding their MOOC learning encounters, tends to be subjective and holds immense value for online education. This study conducted a systematic review of theories, themes, and methods related to online course review analysis. The analysis suggests that there are 12 key themes that constitute a coding framework. for online course review analysis should be encapsulated in its categories. These themes are lecture materials, faculty team, course structure, course content, interaction, assignment and assessment, learner support, technology, instructional approaches, course value, certificate and credits, and course difficulty. With this understanding, scholars would enhance their proficiency in crafting or choosing frameworks. We also evaluate theories and methods related to online course review analysis to comprehend the guiding theoretical perspectives in conducting research and how different methods or technologies can inform decisions for MOOC instructional enhancement.

articleTitle: Under the Condition of Mindfulness Meditation: The Influence of Positive Emotion Design on Multimedia Learning
abstract: This study investigated the impact of positive emotion design on multimedia learning under the condition of mindfulness meditation. Forty-eight students from a university in central China were randomly divided into two groups: a positive emotion design group and a neutral emotion design group. After completing a 10-minute mindfulness meditation training, participants in the two groups took a multimedia course on positive emotion design or neutral emotion design. By using a mixed method of questionnaires and collecting physiological data (EEG and ECG), we further explored the differences between the two groups of participants in terms of their emotional states, cognitive processing, learning outcomes, and subjective experiences. The results showed that under the condition of mindfulness meditation, the positive emotion design group achieved significantly better comprehension scores and marginally significantly higher retention and attention scores compared to the neutral emotion group. The study suggests that the addition of emotional design elements to instructional videos under mindfulness meditation conditions is beneficial to learners’ academic performance.

articleTitle: Exploring Pre-service Science Teachers’ Cognitive and Emotional Patterns in the Video-based Multimodal Analysis Integrated Collective Reflection: an Epistemic Network Analysis
abstract: Collective reflection refers to the process of reflection by group members through social interactions and the results of this process. It has been applied and promoted in teacher education and has become the key to improving teachers’ professional development. Video-based automatic multi-modal analysis technology can analyze teachers’ classroom behavior from an overall, micro, and specific perspective, providing teachers with useful work information. However, current research shows that teachers’ collective reflection lacks in-depth and critical reflection. And few studies have explored how the automated video-based multimodal analysis techniques could be integrated into pre-service science teachers’ collective reflections from the perspective of cognitive and affective changes. Therefore, in order to explore the use of video-based automatic multimodal analysis technology in collective reflection among pre-service science teachers, this study compared collective reflections combined with video-based automatic multimodal analysis reports and collective reflections without analysis reports. Their collective reflective discourse was then encoded based on the pre-trained large language model BERT, and the cognitive and emotional patterns of collective reflection of these pre-service science teachers were visualized through Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA). The results of this study revealed that the pre-service science teachers showed a higher level of cognition in the collective reflection integrated with video multimodal analysis reports. Qualitative data also confirmed that via viewing the discussion on the multimodal analysis reports, the pre-service science teachers achieved more critical and in-depth reflection on their teaching practice and the suggestions for improving their future science teaching.

articleTitle: Application research and hotspot analysis of learning analysis technology in education based on CiteSpace
abstract: With the transformation of education digitization, learning analysis technology has gradually become an important means in the field of education. Based on the literature related to learning analysis technology from 2010 to 2023, this paper reviews the application of learning analysis technology in education. Firstly, the concept, key technologies and tools of learning analysis technology are introduced. Secondly, it elaborates the application of learning analysis technology in education and the existing problems and challenges. Finally, the development prospects and suggestions of learning analysis technology in the field of education are discussed. It is believed that with the continuous development and improvement of technology, learning analysis technology will be more accurate and reliable, bringing more innovation and development opportunities for education.

articleTitle: The relationship between digital literacy and K-12 students’ academic performance: mediation effects of problem-solving ability
abstract: In the digital age, digital literacy has become a necessary skill for contemporary citizens and has received attention from educational researchers. Digital literacy is an important influencing factor that affects students’ learning, fuels the development of students’ thinking, and improves students’ performance. However, the mechanism of how digital literacy affects students’ academic performance has yet to be explored in depth. On this basis, this study used a national large-scale questionnaire survey to construct a model mediated by problem-solving ability and moderated by grade for 8,916 K-12 students. The results show that digital literacy is a significant direct predictor of academic achievement; problem-solving ability has a significant mediating effect on digital literacy and students’ academic achievement. Digital literacy can contribute to the development of K-12 students’ problem-solving ability, thereby improving their academic performance.

articleTitle: The Effects of Positive Emotional Design on Learning Outcomes in Multimedia Learning: A Meta-analysis
abstract: Prior studies on the effects of positive emotional design in multimedia learning environments have shown inconsistent findings. In recent years, physiological devices have steadily been integrated into multimedia learning, and when compared to earlier questionnaires and self-report measures, they may accurately and objectively record learners’ learning processes in real time. Therefore, this paper reviews studies containing physiological measurement data, utilizing meta-analysis to explore the effects of positive emotional design on learners’ positive emotions, physiological data, mental effort, retention performance, transfer performance, and potential moderating variables causing inconsistent results. The results indicate that positive emotional design can facilitate learners’ retention performance (k=15, g=0.22), transfer performance (k=18, g=0.23), and physiological data (k=8, g}=0.49) However, no significant difference in learners’ positive emotions (k=19, g=0.08) and mental effort (k=11, g=0.17). The moderation effects of learners’ transfer performance and attention are not statistically significant. This meta-analysis provides valuable insights for researchers and practitioners, suggesting that positive emotional design in multimedia learning can boost learning performance and attention.

articleTitle: An analysis of engagement dynamic characteristics in a research methods course facilitated by online scaffolding
abstract: Learning engagement is an important factor that effects learning achievement and has dynamic characteristics. However, there is a lack of exploration on the dynamic characteristics of learning engagement. There is a need to analyze student process data to present the dynamic characteristics of learning engagement in online scaffolding context to provide some insights into online scaffolding design. During an 16 weeks semester, a total of 47 student participated in online scaffolding supported learning. Participants’ flow and interactions were collected. A dynamic emotional engagement was also identified in the students’ flow perceptions, which included two cycles of disengagement and re-engagement. Students encountered different challenges that led to disengagement phases, which highlighted the need for specific types of learning scaffolding in learning process. Social network analysis (SNA) revealed that social network density gradually increased with the course. Social network density increased more rapidly in the first half of the semester than in the second half of the semester. Based on this, this study suggests providing dynamic scaffolding for learners to support students’ productive participation in learning according to the dynamic characteristics of student engagement.

articleTitle: An Analysis of the Current Status of Student Teachers’ Digital Literacy
abstract: The rapid development of a new round of digital technology has changed traditional teaching and education methods. As the reserve force of future teachers, the development and cultivation of digital literacy of student teachers is an inevitable requirement for building a high-quality teacher team and cultivating excellent digital talents in the digital era. The purpose of this study was to explore the overall development status of digital literacy among student teachers in central China, and the differences in digital literacy levels among student teachers under different characteristic backgrounds. The results showed that the digital literacy level of student teachers is in the upper middle level, and there are significant differences in digital literacy among student teachers with different genders, grades, and degree types. This finding is beneficial for promoting the balanced and effective development of student teachers’ digital literacy.

articleTitle: A Review of Intervention Practices to Improve Teachers’ Occupational Well-Being
abstract: By reviewing 82 empirical research papers on improving teachers’ occupational well-being published between 2000 and 2022, this review found that most researchers have focused only on teachers’ affective well-being, with particular attention paid to stress and emotional depletion, while less research has been conducted on other dimensions such as social well-being. Most interventions focused on the cognitive restructuring category and faced insufficient incorporation of technology. Based on the review results, we suggest understanding the diversity of teachers’ occupational well-being and finding technological methods to optimize the effectiveness of interventions.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction and Application of Smart Learning Space in Guangzhou Medical University
abstract: The development of artificial intelligence and big data technology presents fresh prospects for the evolution of learning spaces. The establishment of smart learning space addresses the increasing educational requirements of both educators and learners. Taking Guangzhou Medical University as a case study, this study developed a smart learning space model based on constructivism learning theory, multiple intelligence theory and ergonomics theory. We explored the practical application of smart learning space in teaching and assesses their effectiveness through questionnaire survey. This study aims to offer insights and guidance for the design and implementation of smart learning space in educational settings.

articleTitle: Understanding Co-teaching Patterns and Their Influences on Student Engagement in Blended Synchronous Classroom: Through the Lens of Teaching Presence
abstract: Co-teaching is critical to improving the effectiveness of student engagement. However, in the blended synchronous teaching and learning, how online teacher and onsite teacher co-teach is still not clear. This study therefore from the perspective of teaching presence to shed light on the co-teaching patterns and their influences on student engagement in the blended synchronous classroom. The teaching presence framework is applied to outline the essential characteristics of co-teaching presence, and then supports using a lag sequential analysis approach to explore the co-teaching patterns in two representative classrooms (i.e., blended synchronous classroom with high-level co-teaching vs. blended synchronous classroom with low-level co-teaching). Additionally, the student engagement in the two levels of co-teaching classrooms was investigated by questionnaire and was compared. The obtained results highlighted that the contribution of co-teaching in the blended synchronous classroom is reflected in two aspects: the delivery and construction of knowledge, as well as the creation of a harmonious classroom climate. The result also showed that students in the high-level co-teaching classroom performed a higher cognitive engagement than the low-level co-teaching classroom did. Additional findings, implications, limitations, and research directions are discussed.

articleTitle: Crafting Tomorrow’s Evaluations: Assessment Design Strategies in the Era of Generative AI
abstract: In recent years, no other technology has revolutionised our life as Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI). GenAI has gained the attention of a myriad of users in almost every profession. Its advancement has had an intense impact on education, significantly disrupting the assessment design and evaluation methodologies. Despite the potential benefits and possibilities of GenAI in the education sector, there are several concerns primarily centred around academic integrity, authenticity, equity of access, assessment evaluation methodology, and feedback. Consequently, academia is encountering challenges in assessment design that are essential to retaining academic integrity in the age of GenAI. In this article, we discuss the challenges, and opportunities that need to be addressed for the assessment design and evaluation. The article also highlights the importance of clear policy about the usage of GenAI in completing assessment tasks, and also in design approaches to ensure academic integrity and subject learning. Additionally, this article also provides assessment categorisation based on the use of GenAI to cultivate students’ and academic professionals’ knowledge. It also provides information on the skills necessary to formulate and articulate problems and evaluate the task, enabling students and academics to effectively utilise GenAI tools.

articleTitle: Impact of ChatGPT and prompt on pre-service teachers’ technology-enhanced learning design: a mixed method study
abstract: This study explores the effects of ChatGPT and prompt on pre-service teachers’ (PSTs’) technology-enhanced learning (TEL) design ability and learning experiences. Fifty-seven PSTs taking a course named Modern Educational Technology participated in this study, and were randomly assigned to one of the two conditions: (1) a combination of ChatGPT and prompt group; or (2) a ChatGPT-only group. A mixed method was used by rating the quality of PSTs’ TEL design artifacts, combing with the qualitative data from the semi-structure interview. The results indicated that compared with the ChatGPT-only group, the combination of ChatGPT and prompt significantly improved the quality of PSTs’ TEL design artifacts and reduced their extrinsic cognitive loads during the design process. Moreover, the interview results also illustrated that prompt could enhance the efficiency and quality of PSTs’ interactions with ChatGPT. However, PSTs also reported some problems when using prompt such as they exhibited high perceived risk. This study provides practical implications for the application of ChatGPT to pre-service teacher education: Instructors should design proper prompt in advance to help PST better interact with ChatGPT, and thereby improve their learning experience and performance.

articleTitle: Modeling Behavior Change for Multi-model At-Risk Students Early Prediction
abstract: In the educational domain, identifying students at risk of dropping out is essential for allowing educators to intervene effectively, improving both academic outcomes and overall student well-being. Data in educational settings often originate from diverse sources, such as assignments, grades, and attendance records. However, most existing research relies on online learning data and just extracting the quantitative features. While quantification eases processing, it also leads to a significant loss of original information. Moreover, current models primarily identify students with consistently poor performance through simple and discrete behavioral patterns, failing to capture the complex continuity and non-linear changes in student behavior. We have developed an innovative prediction model, MultimodalChangePoint Detection (MCPD), utilizing the textual teacher remark data and numerical grade data from middle schools. Our model achieves a highly integrated and intelligent analysis by using independent encoders to process two types of data, fusing the encoded feature. The model further refines its analysis by leveraging a changepoint detection module to pinpoint crucial behavioral changes, which are integrated as dynamic weights through a simple attention mechanism. Experimental validations indicate that our model achieves an accuracy range of 70-75%, with an average outperforming baseline algorithms by approximately 5-10%. Additionally, our algorithm demonstrates a certain degree of transferability, maintaining high accuracy when adjusted and retrained with different definitions of at-risk, proving its broad applicability.

articleTitle: Research and Practice on the Blended Online and Offline Training Model for Digital Literacy Cultivation of University Teachers
abstract: The level of digital literacy among teachers is decisive for the digital transformation of higher education in China. This study, in response to the main challenges in current digital literacy training for university teachers, such as limited participation time, scarcity of free online training, low effectiveness of face-to-face training, and difficulty in addressing personalized issues, has constructed a “three levels (macro-meso-micro) and two integrations (online-offline integration)” blended online and offline training model over five years of action research in digital literacy enhancement. Based on the institution’s essential needs, ten face-to-face training topics were developed, and digital literacy enhancement MOOCs for these topics were produced. Thirteen rounds of blended online and offline training for digital literacy enhancement training were conducted within the university, achieving significant results and leading to positive promotion and application outside the campus.

Author Keywords: Blended Online and Offline Training Model
