articleTitle: An Investigative Study of Junior High School Students’ Conceptions of AI Learning: A Drawing Analysis-based Approach
abstract: Exploring junior high school students’ perceptions and experiences about AI learning in the age of intelligence is of great significance. In this study, a total of 218 junior high school students’ drawings of their conceptions of AI learning were collected, and the students’ drawings were coded and statistically analysed using the method of drawing analysis, aiming to explore the overall situation and differences in junior high school students’ conceptions of AI learning. The results showed that junior high school students generally perceived that students were in the main body in AI learning and that the learning took place in AI classrooms with good smart facilities. Most students’ learning activities depended on the teacher’s explanations, and most of them showed positive learning emotions. In the dimension of AI learning activities, the grade difference is manifested in that students in the first year of junior high school have more group activities, and students in the second year of junior high school are more inclined to experience various smart products. Gender differences are shown in that male students have more programming tendency and female students rely more on teacher’s explanation.

articleTitle: A Pilot Study on the Development and Validation of AI Literacy Test Items for Grade 7 to Grade 9 Students
abstract: To provide K-12 students with an understanding of AI’s potential opportunities and challenges, AI education has been incorporated into the technology curriculum. Most existing methods for assessing students’ AI literacy rely on self-assessment questionnaires, which may not offer an objective measure of their understanding. This study, therefore, sought to develop and validate a 25 -item multiple-choice test tailored for Hong Kong secondary school students to gauge their AI literacy. A total of 144 students from six secondary schools participated in a pilot test. Item Response Theory (IRT) incorporating a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm, was developed to estimate the difficulty and discrimination indices of test items. The 3-Parameter Logistic (3-PL) model was selected for its effectiveness in providing a more nuanced understanding of item characteristics. Preliminary analysis suggested that the test warrants further revision and enhancement, as evidenced by a Kuder-Richardson Formula 20 (KR-20) reliability coefficient of 0.68. Nonetheless, all test items exhibited satisfactory discrimination capabilities, indicating their proficiency in differentiating among varying levels of respondent aptitude. Thus, this study can provide a foundation for developing a standardized AI literacy test in the future.

articleTitle: Using Museum to Promote Learning for K-12 Students: a Systematic Literature Review from 2003 to 2023
abstract: This study presents a systematic review of 20 years of articles on the usage of museum learning in K-12 education. The study used Scopus as a database source and selected 57 highly relevant articles for detailed coding analysis. The research results indicate that current studies on informal learning outcomes of K-12 children primarily focus on scientific knowledge and emotional attitudes, and most of them carry out empirical studies based on the integration of information technology, such as the combination of AR and educational games, and the combination of AR and mobile devices. In addition, the main research sites are science museums, and the learning content mainly focuses on the fields of physics and biology. This paper also proposes teaching intervention strategies and suggestions to enhance the learning outcomes of K-12 students.

articleTitle: Using fine-grained data to track group effectiveness and individual characteristics of teachers in blended teacher learning
abstract: The deep integration of intelligent technology and educational pedagogy makes teachers face new challenges. Blended teacher learning plays an important role in teacher competence development and teaching innovation. Established studies have focused more on the group cognitive development or individual performance of teachers’ collaborative learning. However, teacher groups and individuals interact with each other in collaborative learning. Therefore, this study utilized cluster analysis, social network analysis, and content analysis to uncover the effects of K-12 teachers’ engagement in blended collaborative learning at the group level and to explore the differences in intrinsic characteristics among groups at the individual level. The results indicated that groups of teachers in face-to-face interactive environments can be categorized into three types based on group engagement effects, which are efficient, strategic, and passive; and that there are differences in characteristics of verbal interaction and competence among individual teachers, which are reflected in reciprocity, centrality, TPACK initial competence, and change among teachers. The study suggests providing teachers with targeted assistance in designing activities, considering the competence of the leader role of the group, and mobilizing teachers to actively participate and accept new knowledge to enhance the effectiveness of the engagement of the groups.

articleTitle: Employ a gamified questioning strategy to facilitate children’s literacy and critical thinking
abstract: Gamified learning has been widely used and regarded as an effective approach in children learning. This study utilized a gamified questioning strategy to facilitate children’s literacy and critical thinking. A gamified reading questioning system has been implemented in many primary schools of Hong Kong for years. Mixed-method research was conducted to explore the effects of the gamified questioning strategy on children’s literacy and critical thinking. First, a quasi-experiment was conducted in one primary school to examine the difference of examination scores at school between users and non-users of the system. Furthermore, thirty-nine top performers from five primary schools were invited to attend a survey (including questionnaires and interviews) and a writing workshop. The results show that the use of gamified questioning strategy can help improve students’ interest and motivation in literacy learning, as well as their literacy competence. Furthermore, the gamified questioning strategy can help develop children’s critical thinking during reading.

articleTitle: A Review of Recommender Systems Based on Video Learning Resources in Online Education
abstract: Compared to texts, videos can better stimulate learners’ learning motivation and keep their attention. Recommender systems based on video learning resources can aid learners in discovering relevant resources by considering the video’s attributes and learners’ preferences. This study follows PRISMA to conduct a literature review of the recommender system based on video learning resources in online education, and retains 27 articles. The analysis concentrated on the primary recommendation methods, data types utilized, evaluation metrics, application effects, and the influence of these systems on learners’ educational experiences. The findings indicate that the design and implementation of video learning resource-based recommender systems are advanced, yielding highly precise recommendations. However, the potential of the video learning resource recommender system to significantly enhance learners’ educational outcomes and its precise operational mechanisms warrant further investigation. Future research are suggested in the end of this study.

articleTitle: What influences college students to drop out of MOOC: A Study Based on Grounded Theory
abstract: MOOC (Massive Open Online Courses), as a new online education resource and course form, has attracted attention from all sides in recent years, and its development trend is rapid. More and more users are choosing to study online courses, with college students being the mainstream of MOOCs. However, the interference and challenges of college students’ online learning are also increasing, and the phenomenon of high dropout rate leads to the poor learning effect and learning experience of college students’ online learning. Therefore, this study adopts the grounded theory research method, obtains data through in-depth interviews, and forms a model of influencing factors of college students’ MOOC dropout behavior through open-axial-selective three-level coding based on bottom-up induction, and expounds the influence of various factors such as learners, courses, teachers and environment on college students’ MOOC dropout behavior. It provides an important theoretical support for people to objectively understand the dropout behavior of college students in MOOC learning and reduce the dropout rate of college students in MOOC learning.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence and Machine (Deep) Learning in Medical Education: A Bibliometric Analysis Based on VOSviewer and CiteSpace
abstract: The complexity of the medical education field often precludes a complete reliance on explanations derived from artificial intelligence (AI). Despite the potential applications of AI, particularly those based on machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), in facilitating instructional support and personalized learning for medical students. Such technologies still confront substantial challenges in accurately comprehending and adapting to the multifaceted nature of medical training processes. Consequently, research into the application of AI in medical education remains an evolving field; however, few bibliometric analyses in the literature have systematically studied this area. To assist academics in grasping the future direction of teaching methodologies and educational strategies within the medical profession, this study aimed to map out the research hotspots and trends of AI and DL within medical education through bibliometric analysis. The Web of Science Core Collection provided 416 articles and reviews in the study period of 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> January 2000 to 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> April 2024. Countries, institutions, authors, references, and keywords in the field were visualized and analyzed using the VOSviewer and CiteSpace.

articleTitle: Is Creative Thinking Really Teachable? A MetaAnalysis Based on 64 Experimental or QuasiExperimental Studies
abstract: Creative thinking has become one of the essential abilities for individuals in the 21 st century. Debate has been ongoing among researchers about whether creative thinking can indeed be taught. This study employs 64 experimental or quasi-experimental studies to explore the teachability of creative thinking through meta-analysis. The results indicate that teaching in all academic fields and at all educational stages can and has enhanced students’ creative thinking. Additionally, this study employs subgroup analysis to investigate the differential impact of moderating variables, such as educational stages, discipline categories, teaching intervention with or without technology, and assessment tools on the effectiveness of teaching creative thinking. The findings reveal: 1) The effectiveness of teaching creative thinking is optimal at the senior high school level. 2) Significant differences exist in the effectiveness of teaching creative thinking across disciplines, with science showing the best results. 3) No significant difference is found in the enhancement of students’ creative thinking with or without technological involvement. 4) Compared to the standardized scale in assessment tools, the improvement in creative thinking ability measured by the self-developed scale is more pronounced.

articleTitle: What did we say in a blended lesson study among expert, in-service and preservice teachers? Exploring the collaborative talk pattern
abstract: As a form of teacher collaboration, lesson study has recently received increasing attention in teacher education. Existing research highlighted the importance of two types of collaboration: one between experts and in-service teachers, and the other between preservice and in-service teachers in a blended lesson study. However, limited research has been conducted on the tripartite collaboration among experts, in-service teachers, and preservice teachers. Nowadays, collaborative talk is often used to explore the collaborative mechanisms within teacher collaboration. In this vein, Pedagogically Productive Talk (PPT) has been employed as a theoretical framework to capture its patterns. This study explored the characteristics of collaborative talk among expert, in-service, and preservice teachers in a blended lesson study through the lens of the PPT framework, employing Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA) as the method of data analysis. This study particularly focused on two scenarios involving different types of experts: one being an academic expert and the other being a teaching expert with extensive teaching experience. Quantitative analysis reveals different patterns of collaborative talk between the two groups, and this study also provided insight that the inclusion of the preservice teacher contributes to the effective conduct of the collaboration mentioned above.

articleTitle: The Role of the Six-hat Thinking Technique on Pre-service Teachers’ Collective Reflection: Lag Sequential Analysis on the Co-regulation Pattern
abstract: Collective reflection has become a rigorous activity in teacher training and professional development. However, there are still some shortcomings in collective reflection, such as confusion in discussion, low efficiency and difficulty in achieving the effect of promoting individual reflection through collective reflection. This study formulated a collective reflection framework integrated with the six thinking hats based upon the consensus among the experts who are familiar with six hats and teacher education. According to the framework, the pre-service teachers reflected in the order of red-white-yellow-black-green-black-green (until there is no new black hat idea) … By applying co-regulation coding scheme and Lag Sequential Analysis (LSA) to analyze the collective reflection behaviors of 14 groups of pre-service teachers performing three rounds of project-based learning on instructional design, this study revealed the co-regulation patterns in the six-hat technique integrated collective reflection in which blue hat was focused. This study also identified differences in the co-regulation process and co-regulation focuses exhibited by high and low performing groups on understanding the essence of the six-hat thinking technique.

articleTitle: Evaluating generative artificial intelligence in answering course-related open questions: A pilot study
abstract: ChatGPT, which has been discussed in public in recent years, was launched in November 2022, with a continuously expanding market size. Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) has been developing rapidly in China. However, we have little knowledge of how well the GAIs are performing at answering course-related open questions, especially in Chinese. Therefore, this study aims to analyze the performances of GAIs in answering course-related open questions from both machine and manual evaluation perspectives. The results from this study showed that GAIs got unsatisfactory scores in this situation. Two different aspects of comparison of GAIs’ scores are discussed. More study on evaluating the performance of GAI is needed to investigate the capabilities of answering course-related open questions in the future.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Course Activities for College Students’ Metacognitive Regulation in Blended Learning Environment
abstract: The development of students’ metacognitive regulation is a crucial challenge in higher education. Despite its positive correlation with academic achievement, critical thinking and problem-solving ability, students often lack sufficient metacognitive regulation to navigate the complexities of college learning and living. This study aimed to explore what impact course activities have on college students in blended learning environment by incorporating a range of strategies such as strategy instruction, recording data with Mini Program, and reflective journals. A single-group pretest-posttest design was adopted, and a convenience sample of 110 first-year students was included in the study. Students’ metacognitive regulation and demographic information were collected before and after the course. Additionally, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 16 students, and the reflective journals submitted by students via the online platform were retrieved for analysis. The results indicated that students’ metacognitive regulation was significantly enhanced after engaging in course activities, especially in monitoring and evaluation. This study offers valuable guidance for instructors to design and implement blended learning activities for the enhancement of students’ metacognitive regulation.

articleTitle: Addressing mental health problems facing marginalized youths through technological interventions: a narrative review
abstract: This study explores the impact of technology on enhancing the mental health of marginalized adolescent groups. With a growing concern over mental health issues among youth, such as depression and anxiety, this research provides timely insight into how digital interventions can offer support. Employing a narrative review methodology, the study synthesizes findings from 66 included studies to examine the breadth and effectiveness of technological applications in mental health interventions. The analysis reveals that technology-based solutions, including mobile applications, online platforms, and digital games, are increasingly being used to address mental health challenges faced by adolescents from various marginalized backgrounds. These technologies cater to different needs and preferences, indicating a diverse approach to mental health support. The findings underscore the potential of technology to bridge gaps in traditional mental health services by offering accessible, engaging, and personalized options for young people. The study concludes that while technology holds promise for enhancing mental health outcomes, further research is needed to optimize its integration into comprehensive care strategies for marginalized youth.

articleTitle: Metaverse improves the learning experiences rather than learning outcomes: Evidence from an experimental study in higher education
abstract: One of the most barriers in online learning is lack of interaction, and the metaverse has emerged as a potential solution to address this challenge. However, empirical research is lacking to verify the actual effectiveness of the educational metaverse. This study an undergraduate class in the Virbela metaverse platform was designed and a quasi-experiment was conducted to investigate the impact of the metaverse on learning outcomes and experiences. The study results showed that the metaverse learning environment could improve students’ learning experience in terms of cognitive and behavioral engagement as well as perceived sociability. The performance of students in the metaverse classroom was, however, inferior to that of students in the face-to-face classroom. The research findings both support and question some previous investigations of learning in virtual reality and thus extend our understanding of metaverse as an innovative online learning space.

articleTitle: What does Artificial Intelligence Generated Content bring to Teaching and Learning? A literature review on AIGC in Education
abstract: In order to inspire future researches and practices regarding the use of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) in education, this study conducted a literature review on AIGC in education. The study found that using AIGC in teaching and learning brings unprecedented opportunities for digital transformation in education, including providing technical support for the enhancement of personalized learning, empowering the cultivation of higher-order cognitive skills, and transforming educational assessment to reshape teaching and learning. Nevertheless, the application of AIGC in education may involve risks such as cognitive biases, ethical concerns, and widening the digital divide. To address the risks, coping strategies have been proposed by researchers, including strengthening the capability of providing reliable AIGC services, developing ethical guidelines for AIGC in education, and promoting teachers’ and students’ digital literacy. However, the existing studies mainly focused on theoretical analyses, and practical researches of AIGC in education is still limited. Based upon the literature review, the authors put forward future research directions for reference.

articleTitle: Exploring the User Experience of Geo-Spatial Tech: CAVE Immersive Augmented Reality Learning in the Geo-Project 1941 Battle of Hong Kong
abstract: During the outbreak of the Pacific War as part of the Second World War, Hong Kong was turned into a battlefield for 18 days. This research project centered around this incident in 1941, utilizing advanced geo-spatial technology to locate and explore the lost relics scattered across various hills in Hong Kong. Since these artifacts are remote from the city and even hiking trails, reaching them poses a certain level of risk. To enhance students’ experience of the artifact environment, we employ technologies to transform it into a Cave Automatic Virtual Environment (CAVE) immersive augmented reality environment. The objective of this paper is to explore and analyze the learning experiences of students who engage with this technology. The analysis reveals that appropriate use of technology and thoughtful instructional design can effectively enhance the Hybrid Geo-CAVE learning environment. Furthermore, comprehensive and holistic learning facilitation, encompassing pre-class, in-class, and post-class support that meets educational needs, is crucial. Additionally, personalized and customized learning delivery designs can align individual differences among students, enhancing their learning effectiveness. Moreover, it is recommended to explore additional hybrid dimensions to create a more dynamic and engaging learning environment that aligns with individual needs and fosters effective learning outcomes.

articleTitle: Integrating Generative AI in Software Engineering Education: Practical Strategies
abstract: The transformative influence of generative artificial intelligence (AI), notably large language models (LLMs), has significantly reshaped the software engineering (SE) landscape, impacting various aspects of software development within industry and academia. The imperative to integrate generative AI into educational programs arises from the necessity to furnish graduates with contemporary methodologies that enhance software quality and streamline development processes. Nevertheless, a research gap exists concerning the systematic integration of established SE education guidelines with specific course contexts to strengthen SE education through incorporating generative AI. In response to this gap, our study presents a vision for integrating generative AI into SE education, with a particular emphasis on practical integration strategies aimed at endowing students with essential competencies tailored for contemporary software development. Aligning our vision with the knowledge domains within SE education, we delineate its application across specific areas such as code generation, auto test case completion, and others. The overall objective of these proposed initiatives is to furnish students in SE with an updated and immersive learning experience, thereby addressing the evolving demands of the field.

articleTitle: Role-Playing in Online International Chinese Collaborative Learning: A Framework Based on Activity Theory
abstract: This paper aims to apply activity theory to develop a structured framework for designing online collaborative activities in international Chinese language education. The framework innovatively integrates role-playing as a primary strategy for role assignment within collaborative activities. Additionally, the paper evaluates the effectiveness of this framework in real teaching scenarios, offering both theoretical and practical guidance for collaborative teaching activity design in the field of online international Chinese language instruction.

articleTitle: Using Chatbots to teach English as a foreign language: A systematic literature review from 2010 to 2023
abstract: This study conducts a systematic review of the research on the utilization of chatbots for supporting English as a Foreign Language (EFL) instruction in K-12 and higher education settings from 2010 to 2023. The study adheres to the PRISMA methodology guidelines and searches open access empirical studies in three renowned databases: Web of Science, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore. Ultimately, a total of 42 empirical studies are selected as the research sample library for this comprehensive review. The analysis focuses on four interconnected aspects of chatbot-supported EFL teaching: instructional context, instructional design, technical features, and application effects. The findings unveil current research trends and shed light on the teaching environment surrounding chatbots in EFL instruction. Furthermore, this review highlights the technological affordances offered by chatbots while reporting both their effects and limitations based on existing studies. Finally, new avenues for future research in chatbot-based EFL instruction are proposed.
